Revised: July 16, 2026. 685 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics Ribka Devina Margaretha1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited. This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025. Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions. Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98. Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values. Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis. Keywords: Dengue fever, Sentiment-based network analysis, Spatial analysis, Temporal analysis, Social media. 1. Introduction Dengue fever remains one of the fastest- spreading vector-borne diseases and a major global public health challenge, endemic in more than 100 countries and threatening approximately 3.9 billion people, particularly in Southeast Asia and Latin America [1-3]. In Indonesia, dengue is highly endemic and continues to cause serious health problems, with more than 257,000 reported cases and over 1,400 deaths in 2024 [4]. The increasing spread of dengue, driven by climate change, urbanisation, and population growth, has also heightened public concern regarding outbreaks and prevention efforts [5]. The growing use of social media, particularly Twitter, has created new opportunities to observe public responses and information exchange related to disease outbreaks[6-8]. Through mentions, replies, and reposts, Twitter enables rapid information diffusion across communities, while certain accounts play disproportionately influential roles in shaping discussions [9]. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has therefore been widely applied to identify influential actors and examine information diffusion dynamics within online networks [10, 11]. Beyond interaction patterns, social media discussions also reflect public opinions and emotional responses toward ongoing health issues [12]. Sentiment analysis provides a complementary approach for capturing these perceptions, and incorporating sentiment information into network analysis can deepen understanding of how dengue- related discussions propagate and evolve on social media [13]. Dengue burden and public health responses are not uniformly distributed across Indonesia, with substantial disparities observed across provinces and Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 686 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ regions due to differences in population density, climate conditions, healthcare accessibility, and vector control capacity [14, 15]. Public perceptions and responses to health information also vary across communities due to cultural and social differences [16]. These regional variations highlight the importance of incorporating spatial information to better understand geographic differences in dengue- related discussions, public sentiment, and information dissemination patterns. Previous studies have applied SNA to identify influential users and examine information diffusion in online discussions, while sentiment analysis has been widely used to understand public perceptions toward health-related issues, and spatial analysis has been employed to reveal geographic variations in dengue transmission and public health responses. However, these approaches are typically investigated in isolation, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how interaction structures, public sentiment, and geographic context collectively shape online discussions. Studies integrating sentiment-weighted social networks with spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter remain particularly limited, highlighting the need for a more integrated analytical framework. To address this gap, this study integrates sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related Twitter discussions, constructing sentiment-weighted interaction networks and analysing them alongside geographic and temporal dimensions. The specific contributions of this study are: • Analysis of the spatial distribution of discussions and sentiments across Indonesian cities • Construction of sentiment-based interaction networks capturing both communication structure and public perception • Identification of national-level influential users using PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality • Identification of regional influential users across multiple Indonesian cities • Analysis of temporal discussion patterns and sentiment dynamics • Visualisation of interaction networks illustrating information diffusion structures. The remainder of this paper is structured as follows. Section 2 reviews related literature. Section 3 describes the data and methodology. Section 4 presents the results and discussion. Section 5 summarises the findings and outlines future directions. 2. Related works 2.1 Social network analysis for information diffusion SNA has been widely applied to investigate information diffusion and interaction patterns in online social networks, modelling users as nodes and interactions as edges to identify influential actors and community structures [17]. Various approaches have been proposed for influencer detection, including the NetDegree centrality measure and the Weighted Correlated Influence (WCI) model combining user activity and network topology [18, 19]. SNA has also been applied to explore community structures and communication dynamics in domain-specific discussions [20]. In health-related contexts, SNA has been used to identify key influencers, dominant topics, and communication structures shaping public awareness [10, 11, 21]. However, most existing health-related SNA studies focus on network topology and influencer identification without incorporating sentiment context or geographic variation. Bonifazi et al. identified influential users in COVID-19 vaccine Twitter discourse through a multilayer network approach, but did not construct sentiment-segmented networks or examine geographic distributions [21]. Durmaz and Hengirmen applied SNA to vaccine- related Twitter discourse in Turkey using in-degree and betweenness centrality, but did not integrate sentiment labels or examine spatial distributions [22]. Pratiwi et al. combined SNA and sentiment analysis for asthma-related Twitter discourse, but did not link findings to geographic distributions or construct sentiment-segmented networks [10]. The absence of sentiment integration and spatial context in these studies limits the depth of understanding achievable in health-related discourse analysis. 2.2 Sentiment analysis in social media discussions Sentiment analysis is widely applied to understand public opinions in social media, with recent studies demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced language models including IndoBERT for Indonesian-language content [23, 24]. Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan have incorporated sentiment into network-based analyses for influential user identification [25, 26]. However, applications combining sentiment and network characteristics in health-related discussions remain limited. Dengue-specific sentiment studies such as Abdul Ghani et al. demonstrate the value of sentiment for disease surveillance but do not Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 687 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ construct interaction networks or link findings to geographic distributions [27]. Indonesian-language classification studies such as Supriyadi and Makatita and Nabiilah et al. demonstrate strong model performance without connecting findings to network structures or spatial patterns [23, 24]. While Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan incorporate sentiment into network analyses, neither examined dengue- related discourse or linked findings to spatial distributions [25, 26]. No prior study has simultaneously applied sentiment-integrated SNA to dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data, leaving a gap in understanding how emotional responses and interaction structures collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.3 Spatial analysis in health-related studies Spatial analysis has gained increasing attention in public health and social media research for understanding geographic variations in behaviour and information dissemination. Lovera and Cardinale demonstrated that geolocation enriches the interpretation of social media discussions [34]. Similarly, Wu et al. highlighted the value of geospatial enrichment for understanding large-scale sentiment behaviour[35]. In health-related contexts, Lin et al. revealed linguistic and geographic disparities in COVID-19 public awareness through social media, while Zhang et al. applied geographical and temporal analysis to health-related tweets to identify spatiotemporal disease discussion patterns at regional level [36, 37]. However, these studies focus on geographic distribution patterns without modelling user interaction networks or identifying regional-level influential users. Lin et al., Zhang et al., Lovera and Cardinale, and Wu et al. all incorporate geolocation into social media analysis, but do not construct interaction networks, identify influential users, or examine how sentiment varies across network communities [z-37]. Studies applying spatial analysis to dengue-related social media discourse, such as Abdul Ghani et al., have similarly focused on geographic mapping without modelling user interaction dynamics or examining sentiment- segmented network structures [27]. The absence of interaction network modelling and sentiment integration limits understanding of how network dynamics and public sentiment collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.4 Research gap Despite the established contributions of SNA, sentiment analysis, and spatial analysis individually, existing health-related social media studies address these dimensions in isolation, as demonstrated across Sections 2.1 to 2.3, focusing on network topology without sentiment context [10, 21, 22], applying sentiment classification without network or spatial linkage[23, 27], or examining geographic patterns without modelling interaction dynamics [34-37]. While sentiment analysis and network approaches have each been applied to health-related social media discourse individually, their simultaneous integration with spatial analysis in the specific context of dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data remains unexplored. No prior study has proposed a unified framework simultaneously capturing the structural, emotional, and geographic dimensions of dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter. This study addresses that gap by integrating sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis within a single framework, constructing sentiment- segmented interaction networks to examine how different emotional contexts shape network structure and influencer profiles, mapping discussion distributions and regional influencer patterns across Indonesian cities, and tracing temporal dynamics of both discussion volume and sentiment evolution over a five-year period. This integrated approach offers a more complete understanding of information dissemination patterns, influential users, and public perceptions across different locations and time periods than prior single-method studies have provided. 3. Materials and method 3.1 Dataset Dengue-related tweets were collected from Twitter (X) between January 2021 and December 2025 using the Scweet Python library with three keywords: "dbd" (dengue haemorrhagic fever acronym in Indonesian), "Aedes aegypti" (the dengue-carrying mosquito species), and "demam berdarah dengue" (dengue haemorrhagic fever). Data collection was conducted between 9-14 April 2026. The collected tweets span the period from January 2021 to December 2025, reflecting the full range of historical tweets retrievable through Scweet at the time of collection; Scweet retrieves historical tweets via browser automation rather than the official Twitter/X API, and collection completeness is therefore subject to the platform's search indexing and any rate-limiting constraints encountered during scraping. All tweets included in this study represent observed data retrieved directly through Scweet; no Received: June 15, 2026. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ projected, simulated, or placeholder records are included in the dataset or in any reported analysis. Collection was conducted as a series of discrete scraping sessions per keyword and sub-period, with no session returning a tweet count at or exceeding the configured retrieval limit (500-1,000 tweets, depending on keyword), indicating retrieval without truncation within each queried window. A completeness check was performed by examining the year-by-year distribution of collected tweets to confirm the absence of anomalous gaps or artificially uniform collection patterns; as detailed in Section 4.6.1, tweet volume varied organically across the five-year period, consistent with externally documented dengue activity patterns in Indonesia rather than indicating systematic data loss. Each tweet record contains textual content, publication date, user information, engagement statistics, and interaction attributes including mentions, replies, and reposts. The collected dataset serves as the primary source for all sentiment, network, spatial, and temporal analyses conducted in this study. 3.2 Method This study employs an integrated analytical framework consisting of data preprocessing, sentiment classification, network construction, community detection, spatial analysis, and temporal analysis. The overall research procedure is illustrated in Fig. 1. Figure. 1 Overall research procedure flowchart Received: June 15, 2026. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ 3.2.1. Data preprocessing The datasets collected from different periods were combined and filtered to retain only the attributes required for analysis, including tweet identifiers, usernames, tweet content, timestamps, language information, location attributes, and interaction metadata. User mentions and replies were extracted separately to support network construction. Duplicate tweets and records with missing values in essential attributes were removed, and tweet texts were cleaned through lowercasing, URL removal, mention and hashtag removal, number and punctuation removal, and whitespace normalisation. Tweets that became empty after cleaning were discarded, and only Indonesian-language tweets were retained. Examples of tweets before and after preprocessing are shown in Table 1. For spatial analysis, location information was obtained from tweet-level and user profile locations, with the latter used as a fallback when tweet-level location was unavailable. Location texts were normalised and matched against a reference dataset of Indonesian cities, with common aliases and abbreviations standardised to improve matching accuracy. This process successfully mapped 3,327 tweets (58.22%) to 168 Indonesian cities. 3.2.2. Sentiment analysis Sentiment analysis was conducted to identify public opinions expressed in dengue-related Twitter discussions. Two pretrained Indonesian sentiment classification models from the Hugging Face library, namely w11wo/indonesian-roberta-base-sentiment- classifier [28] and taufiqdp/indonesian-sentiment (fine-tuned from IndoBERT) [29], were applied to the full cleaned dataset (5,715 tweets) as candidates. title_zh: 通过基于情感的网络分析、空间映射和时间动态检查印度尼西亚 Twitter 上与登革热相关的信息传播
source_body_en: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.
abstract_zh: 登革热 仍然是印度尼西亚的一项重大公共卫生挑战,但整合情感分析、社交网络分析和空间分析来检查社交媒体上登革热相关信息传播的研究仍然有限。这项研究提出了一个综合框架,应用于 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间从印度尼西亚 Twitter 收集的 5,715 条登革热相关推文。使用 IndoBERT 进行的情感分类显示,主要是中性话语 (65.23%),有意义的负面言论(20.31%) 和正 (14.45%) 比例。构建和建立了情感加权交互网络,揭示了高度碎片化的结构,模块化得分超过 0.98。医疗保健专业人员通过介数中心性成为最具影响力的参与者,基于 PageRank 的影响力以自循环 治疗 为条件,而卫生部拥有最高的入度值。空间分析,主要基于用户自我报告位置、表明爪哇-巴厘岛走廊沿线的地理集中度以及时间分析显示 1 月和 6 月反复出现的高峰与印度尼西亚的雨季和登革热 暴发 周期一致。这些发现证明了整合情绪、网络和空间维度对于全面公共卫生传播分析的价值。
